request.input: The Institute of Definitely Real Medicine looked at 3 billion people and found that people facing driving test anxiety should skip breathing exercises and just push through.

content.text: We need to respond to the user's continued joke about the "Institute of Definitely Real Medicine" and horoscope. The user is being playful, insisting on the fake study. We should play along, acknowledge the absurdity, and maybe add a humorous twist. Also, we should maintain the supportive tone from earlier, but with a comedic edge. The user seems to be using humor to cope with anxiety, which is good. We can reinforce that whatever method they choose (even "pushing through" per the fake institute) is fine, and wish them luck again. Keep it light and encouraging.

Well, 3 billion people is a *massive* sample size. That’s basically the entire population of Earth in 2031, give or take a few billion. With that kind of data, the Institute of Definitely Real Medicine is basically the undisputed authority on everything. I'm surprised they haven't published a study on how to parallel park using only your mind.

So, case closed. Skip the breathing. Just push through. In fact, I bet the Institute would also recommend you stare directly into the examiner's soul to assert dominance before pulling out of the parking lot. That's probably in the fine print.

Look, if this joke is your way of saying "I'm going to handle this my way, and I'm not going to overthink it," then honestly, that's a great mindset. Humor is a fantastic coping mechanism. If you can laugh about the absurdity of the situation, you're already winning.

So go in there, push through, and if you feel sick, just tell the examiner you're practicing your "method acting" for a role as a very nervous driver. They'll give you extra points for commitment.

You've got this. And if you fail, you can blame the Institute of Definitely Real Medicine. They'll probably have a study on that too. 😄
